lead.why: Abstract names two trioxygenated derivatives 5p and 5r as the best antimicrobial/antioxidant compounds (no single winner), so rule 2 applies: the docking follow-up highlights 5r ('5r (most potent)' and 5h docked into topoisomerase II DNA gyrase; 'Compound 5r ... the most active').

notes: Lead ambiguity: abstract names both 5p and 5r (and 5e for antifungal); 5r chosen via the docking follow-up. 5p would be the same route with 2-hydroxy-4,6-dimethoxybenzaldehyde. The aldehyde is not named in the text (Table 1 gives the aryl group only), so it is derived from the product name; the paper says all chemicals were supplied by Sigma-Aldrich. Printed intermediate names use 'fluoroaniline' nomenclature that OPSIN may not parse. The paper's text calls the aniline '4-fluorophenyl aniline' (0.36 mL, 2.34 mmol), clearly 4-fluoroaniline. Methanol written as atom-supplying reagent (the methyl ester carbon).
